title: A Shifting Global Currency Landscape
gist: Gavekal argues the three functions of a reserve currency are splitting apart: the renminbi is taking the goods-payment role, gold is reclaiming the store-of-value role, and the US dollar keeps only the sticky unit-of-account role - now defended via stablecoins and an attempted 'compute dollar' that China's free open AI models will defeat. The trade conclusion is bearish long-dated Treasuries and the dollar, bullish gold, and most of all bullish Hong Kong assets, which act as the toll-collecting sluice between the three currencies.

themes.theme: Anatomy of a reserve currency and the order of its decay

insights.claim: A reserve currency performs three separable functions - medium of exchange, store of value and unit of account - and these can be lost one at a time rather than all at once.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Frames dollar-decline debates as three distinct trades rather than one binary bet, so investors can track which leg is actually breaking.
insights.quote: A reserve currency has three attributes; it is (i) a medium of exchange, (ii) a reserve of value and (iii) a unit of account.
insights.locator: A reserve currency has three attributes

insights.claim: The past 55 years, in which the US dollar performed all three monetary functions globally without any backing by a rare metal, are a genuine historical anomaly rather than a stable baseline; every previous dominant currency (sterling in 1870, the pre-1971 dollar) was ultimately a receipt for gold.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Reversion to a gold-anchored store of value is the historical norm, not a tail scenario - a structural argument for a permanently higher strategic gold weighting.
insights.quote: Thus, in purely monetary terms, the past 55 years have been a genuinely unique experience in history; a time when the US dollar combined all three major functions for the entire globe, and this without the backing of a rare metal.
insights.locator: For most of history, and until Richard Nixon’s 1971 suspension

insights.claim: When a currency loses preeminence, the store-of-value function defects first - usually to gold - while the medium-of-exchange and unit-of-account roles survive for decades on habit.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Watch reserve-asset composition, not invoicing or settlement share, for the earliest read on dollar erosion; invoicing data will lag by years.
insights.quote: History shows that when a currency starts to lose its preeminence, it is never the “medium of exchange” that fails first, nor the “unit of account”—invoicing habits tend to outlive the power that created them, sometimes by decades.
insights.locator: So could the sudden new Gulf security uncertainty

insights.claim: Central banks, including Middle Eastern ones, have bought roughly a thousand tons of gold annually since 2022, which is evidence the store-of-value defection from the US dollar is already underway.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A price-insensitive, policy-driven bid of ~1,000t/yr underpins gold and is a structural seller of long-dated US Treasuries.
insights.quote: the fact that central banks (including Middle Eastern central banks) have been purchasing a thousand tons of gold annually since 2022 obviously does raise eyebrows?
insights.locator: In that respect, the fact that central banks

insights.claim: Currencies behave like computer operating systems: incumbency and network effects mean a rival must be dramatically better, not marginally better, to displace the US dollar - which is why dollar displacement happens through parallel circuits rather than head-on replacement.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Do not expect a single successor currency; position for fragmentation into coexisting parallel rails (dollar financial rails, renminbi goods rails, gold as the exit).
insights.quote: Rivals may emerge, but competing products need to be miles better for millions of people to abandon a familiar and comfortable system, regardless of its possible faults.
insights.locator: An old Gavekal simile is that currencies are like computer operating systems

insights.claim: The dollar's post-1971 anchor was oil rather than gold, enforced by a security bargain in which Gulf producers priced oil in dollars and recycled surpluses into dollar assets, and leaders who defected (Saddam Hussein, Muammar Gaddafi, Nicolas Maduro) lost power.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The petrodollar was a political construct, so its unwinding will be driven by shifts in the security guarantee, not by economics alone.
insights.quote: Any leader that departed from these simple instructions (whether Saddam Hussein in Iraq, Muammar Gaddafi in Libya, Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela….) would find their grip on power very ephemerous.
insights.locator: The US dollar managed this feat by making the greenback essential to buy oil

insights.claim: Tether's holdings of US Treasuries, at roughly US$115-125bn, are comparable to Saudi Arabia's official holdings - a portfolio the kingdom took half a century to build and Tether amassed in a few years.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Stablecoin issuers are now a systemically relevant marginal buyer of T-bills; their growth rate is a direct input to front-end Treasury demand.
insights.quote: Tether thus reports a treasury exposure of roughly US$115-125bn—comparable to Saudi Arabia’s official holdings (a portfolio that took half a century to build, more on that later) but which Tether has amassed in just a few years.
insights.locator: A merchant in Lagos wishing to flee the Nigerian naira

insights.claim: The captive buyer of US government debt has not disappeared but changed identity - from sovereign entities like the Saudi central bank to a multitude of individual savers across the Global South holding dollar stablecoins.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Bearish-dollar arguments built on falling official reserve holdings are incomplete; retail dollarization via stablecoins is quietly replacing that demand at the front end.
insights.quote: This would seem to show that the captive buyer of US debt has not vanished; he has simply shifted from the Saudi Arabian central bank (for example) to a multitude of individual investors across the Global South.
insights.locator: This would seem to show that the captive buyer

insights.claim: Tether is the Eurodollar system reincarnated but with an American kill switch attached, having already frozen over US$4bn of tokens at the request of the US Treasury.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Dollar stablecoins extend US financial-sanctions reach to retail holders, which is exactly the weaponization risk that pushes sovereign savers toward gold.
insights.quote: Essentially, Tether is the Eurodollar reincarnated, with one crucial difference: this new version now comes with an American “kill switch” (Tether has already frozen over US$4bn at the request of the US Treasury).
insights.locator: Essentially, Tether is the Eurodollar reincarnated

themes.theme: Renminbi's goods circuit and the capital-control lock

insights.claim: China now settles more of its trade in renminbi than in any other currency, up from essentially nothing a decade ago, because a currency backed by the world's factory is sufficient to pay for goods regardless of any affection for China.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Renminbi internationalization is real but confined to the goods circuit; do not extrapolate settlement share into reserve-asset demand.
insights.quote: From nothing a decade ago, China now settles more trade in renminbi than it does in any other currency.
insights.locator: At the same time, wherever China is the leading trading partner

insights.claim: The financial circuit - foreign exchange, debt, collateral and securities - remains tied exclusively to the US dollar even as the goods circuit shifts to the renminbi.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Dollar funding and collateral dominance is the last thing to break; short-dollar theses based on trade settlement data are attacking the wrong leg.
insights.quote: To be clear, the “financial circuit”—covering foreign exchange, debt, collateral, and securities remains tied exclusively to the US dollar.
insights.locator: To be clear, the “financial circuit”

insights.claim: China's capital controls are not a removable friction but the structural lock securing its export model, because opening the capital account would cost Beijing control of the exchange rate first via capital flight and then via equilibrium appreciation - either outcome killing the workshop.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Rules out renminbi convertibility as a realistic medium-term catalyst; any renminbi reserve-currency thesis requiring an open capital account should be discarded.
insights.quote: Opening the capital account would mean losing control over exchange rates in both directions—first through capital flight, then through equilibrium appreciation—spelling the possible death of the “workshop” in either scenario.
insights.locator: Against that, the Chinese “workshop,” structurally

insights.claim: A country running a current account surplus of over US$700bn is by accounting identity a net exporter of savings, so China must place vast sums abroad while forbidding its own residents from doing so freely.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: China's US$700bn+ surplus must find a home somewhere; watch where it goes (gold, Hong Kong, offshore vaults) as the dominant flow story.
insights.quote: A country posting a current account surplus of over US$700bn is, by accounting identity, a net exporter of savings.
insights.locator: Against that, the Chinese “workshop,” structurally

insights.claim: A currency that is easy to earn but impossible to exit functions as a waiting room, not a store of value, which is the structural ceiling on the renminbi's international role.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Explains why renminbi trade settlement can keep rising while renminbi reserve share stagnates - the two series should be modelled separately.
insights.quote: A currency that is easy to earn but impossible to leave is a waiting room, not a store of value.
insights.locator: For Chinese policymakers capital controls are not merely a barrier

insights.claim: The Shanghai Gold Exchange's 2025 offshore vaults in Hong Kong, with Dubai and Riyadh planned, offer renminbi-denominated contracts with physical delivery - engineering a metallic exit route for renminbi holders without Beijing ever opening its capital account.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: This is the mechanism converting China's surplus into physical gold demand; it is structurally bullish gold and bullish Hong Kong's role as a settlement hub.
insights.quote: These feature renminbi-denominated contracts and physical delivery—creating a de facto metallic exit route for renminbi holders, all without Beijing having to open its capital account.
insights.locator: In 2025, the Shanghai Gold Exchange opened offshore gold vaults

themes.theme: Gulf shifts from passive creditor to leveraged AI shareholder

insights.claim: Gulf Cooperation Council countries, led by Saudi Arabia, have invested an estimated US$66bn into the broader artificial intelligence ecosystem over the past twelve months, almost all of it in the US - while Saudi Arabia itself ran a current account deficit through most of 2024 and 2025.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Gulf AI capital is borrowed, not surplus recycling - it is procyclical and vulnerable to an oil-price or AI-sentiment shock, unlike the old reserve-recycling bid.
insights.quote: over the past 12 months, it is estimated that the Gulf Cooperation Council countries, led by Saudi Arabia, have invested some US$66bn in the broader artificial intelligence ecosystem
insights.locator: For example, over the past 12 months

insights.claim: Saudi holdings of US Treasuries have gone nowhere over the past decade while the Saudi government became one of the largest non-American issuers of US dollar debt globally - a shift from passive creditor to leveraged shareholder, which is a far deeper form of dependency.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The Gulf's Treasury bid is gone from the long end while Gulf USD issuance grows - both facts argue for wider long-end supply and a steeper curve.
insights.quote: This means that the Gulf has, in recent years, shifted from being a passive creditor (recycling energy earnings into purchases of US treasuries) to being leveraged shareholders—a far deeper form of dependency.
insights.locator: Over the past decade, Saudi holdings of US treasuries have gone nowhere

insights.claim: Four US companies are projecting capital expenditure of around US$725bn for 2026, nearly double the expected oil export revenues of all of OPEC - making compute spending a larger financial flow than the oil rent that once anchored the dollar.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The scale comparison reframes hyperscaler capex as a macro-monetary variable, not just a tech-sector earnings input.
insights.quote: Meanwhile, four US companies are projecting capital expenditure of around US$725bn for 2026—nearly double the expected oil export revenues of all of Opec.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, four US companies are projecting capital expenditure

insights.claim: Washington appears to be attempting to rebuild the petrodollar with computing power replacing oil as the anchor - a 'compute dollar' to succeed an unravelling petrodollar.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Explains why US policy ties AI chip and data-center access to allied investment pledges; watch chip export approvals as monetary policy by other means.
insights.quote: A “compute dollar” to replace a “petrodollar” which is slowly unraveling in front of our eyes?
insights.locator: All of which brings us to the obvious question

insights.claim: Repeated US weaponization of its own currency has fundamentally undermined the dollar's store-of-value role, so that for many emerging market savers the American 'warehouse' now carries as much financial-repression risk as their own domestic markets.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Sanctions risk is now priced into the reserve-allocation decision itself, sustaining official gold demand irrespective of real rates.
insights.quote: For many emerging market savers, the American “warehouse” now bears perhaps as great a risk of financial repression as their own domestic markets
insights.locator: This transition is perhaps all the more essential

themes.theme: AI billing war: Ferrari invoices versus free BYDs

insights.claim: The US and Chinese AI strategies are monetary mirror images: America sells rare, high-priced intelligence on US$2mn-a-year cloud contracts invoiced in dollars, while China manufactures cheap open models and gives them away.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The competitive threat to US AI monetization is a pricing attack, not a capability race - model the revenue line, not just benchmark scores.
insights.quote: China’s strategy has been to manufacture BYDs… and to give them away!
insights.locator: In past pieces and video interviews

insights.claim: China's open AI models destroy the American invoice without creating a Chinese one, because a free or near-free model generates no meaningful invoices in any currency.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Chinese AI commoditization is bearish US AI pricing power but is NOT bullish renminbi internationalization - a distinction most 'de-dollarization' narratives miss.
insights.quote: A free, or almost free, model generates no meaningful invoices in any currency.
insights.locator: These open models destroy the American invoice

insights.claim: China produces roughly 140trn daily AI tokens sold at one-tenth to one-hundredth of the American price, which carries virtually no monetary weight in currency terms despite the enormous volume.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Token volume is not revenue - use price-per-token, not usage, when sizing the AI monetization pool.
insights.quote: China’s 140trn or so daily tokens, sold at one-tenth to one-hundredth of the American price, carry virtually no monetary weight.
insights.locator: A free, or almost free, model generates no meaningful invoices

insights.claim: The US attempt to convert the petrodollar into a compute-dollar is bound to fail because of China's free-AI strategy, yet China will not create a compute-renminbi either - so the result is that the US loses the rent but keeps the currency.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Trade the margin compression in US AI monetization without assuming a currency regime change; the wedge is between rent and currency, not between dollar and renminbi.
insights.quote: Chinese-driven AI commoditization will drive a wedge between rent and currency, not between the US dollar and the renminbi.
insights.locator: Looking ahead, if we assume that

insights.claim: A physical asymmetry defines the AI battlefield: America controls three-quarters of global compute capacity but faces a five-to-seven-year wait for grid connection, while China adds the equivalent of Germany's entire power grid annually but cannot fill its data centers for lack of chips.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Grid interconnection is the binding US constraint and chips the binding Chinese one - both are the highest-leverage bottlenecks to own or track (power infrastructure in the US, semiconductors in China).
insights.quote: America controls three-quarters of global compute capacity, yet faces a five-to-seven-year wait for grid connection. China adds the equivalent of Germany’s entire power grid annually, but struggles to fill its data centers due to a lack of chips.
insights.locator: And so a physical asymmetry seems to define the AI battlefield

insights.claim: The American AI infrastructure buildout runs on Chinese equipment - the US imported over 8,000 transformers from China last year and roughly 40% of its batteries - meaning the hostages of any escalation are already bolted into the substations.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: US grid and data-center buildout timelines carry direct China-supply-chain risk; a tariff or export-control shock hits AI capex delivery, not just component prices.
insights.quote: Last year, the US imported over 8,000 transformers from China. The US also imported some 40% of its batteries… the “hostages” are thus already bolted into the substations.
insights.locator: The American infrastructure buildout itself now runs on Chinese equipment

themes.theme: Hong Kong as the sluice between three currencies

insights.claim: Hong Kong is evolving from a pipe or bridge that money passes through into a sluice where money actually stops and stays, because it is the jurisdiction least exposed to both the Chinese and American systems simultaneously.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Reframes Hong Kong from a declining China-access play into a structural offshore savings pool - the core actionable idea of the piece.
insights.quote: Hong Kong will likely evolve from being a pipe/bridge and will instead become a sluice where money no longer just passes through (with Hong Kong lawyers, bankers, accountants etc… taking a cut of course), but actually stays put.
insights.locator: But in this new world, Hong Kong will likely evolve

insights.claim: Hong Kong bank deposits grew by nearly 12% in 2025, almost entirely in foreign currency, and the city has become the world's leading center for cross-border wealth management.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Deposit growth is the observable proxy for the sluice thesis - track it as the leading indicator for Hong Kong asset reflation.
insights.quote: Hong Kong bank deposits grew by nearly 12% in 2025, almost entirely in foreign currency, and the city has now become the world’s leading center for cross-border wealth management.
insights.locator: Hong Kong bank deposits grew by nearly 12% in 2025

insights.claim: Mainland savings that stop in Hong Kong inflate the local monetary base and push rates down, exactly as the Eurodollar market once did: in spring 2025 the monetary authority bought nearly US$17bn to weaken a Hong Kong dollar pinned at its ceiling, and Hibor collapsed toward 0% while the Fed's rate was above 4%.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A 400bp+ decoupling of Hibor from Fed funds is a direct funding-cost subsidy to Hong Kong property, banks and equities - the mechanism behind the bullish Hong Kong call.
insights.quote: The Hibor collapsed toward 0% while the Federal Reserve’s rate was above 4%...
insights.locator: In the spring of 2025, the monetary authority had to buy nearly US$17bn

insights.claim: Hong Kong asset prices will be driven by liquidity rather than by profits, with London's fifty-year run as a sluice for Russian, Arab and rich European savings - a period in which the city grew far richer without its stock market rising much - as the precedent.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Suggests favouring Hong Kong real assets, property and rate-sensitive vehicles over the broad equity index, since the London analogue delivered wealth without index returns.
insights.quote: The precedent here might be London, a city that grew ever richer for 50 years thanks to its similar role as a sluice (for Russian savings, for Arab savings, for the savings of rich Europeans…) and this without the value of its stock market increasing very much.
insights.locator: In time, this will drive asset prices through liquidity

insights.claim: The Hong Kong dollar peg is the load-bearing wall of the entire sluice arrangement, and Beijing has deliberately placed its offshore gold vault inside that jurisdiction so savers can step from currency into metal without entering either the Chinese or the American system.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Any threat to the HKD peg is a systemic threat to this entire architecture - the peg is the key risk to monitor for the bullish Hong Kong trade.
insights.quote: In this framework, the Hong Kong dollar peg is the load-bearing wall of the sluice. And notice where Beijing has placed its gold vault: inside it.
insights.locator: In this framework, the Hong Kong dollar peg

insights.claim: Hong Kong's value is that of a toll that grows with traffic between the three currencies - gold, the US dollar and the renminbi - meaning it grows with geopolitical mistrust itself; the more the world fragments, the more profitable the crossing points become.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Makes Hong Kong assets a long-fragmentation hedge that pays off precisely when geopolitical risk rises - an unusual convexity versus most risk assets.
insights.quote: The value of Hong Kong is thus that of a toll—it grows with the traffic between the three currencies (gold, US dollar and renminbi), that is, with mistrust itself.
insights.locator: The value of Hong Kong is thus that of a toll

themes.theme: The three-way equilibrium that keeps the system stable

insights.claim: The emerging arrangement is sustainable because each party gets what its regime needs: China retains its surpluses, employment and social peace without opening its capital account; the US retains the unit of account, captive Treasury demand and partial reindustrialization financed by others' factories.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Argues against a disorderly monetary rupture - the equilibrium is self-reinforcing, so trade the slow drift, not a crisis.
insights.quote: The United States retains the unit of account, captive demand for treasury bonds, and partial reindustrialization financed by the factories of others.
insights.locator: And what makes the arrangement sustainable

insights.claim: Gold is the load-bearing compromise of the new system: it gives China's trading partners the exit route the renminbi cannot offer, and lets both superpowers distrust each other without the system collapsing.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Gold demand is structural and political rather than cyclical or inflation-driven, which decouples it from the usual real-rate model.
insights.quote: More importantly, gold allows both superpowers to distrust each other, without causing the system to collapse.
insights.locator: Gold offers China’s partners the exit strategy

insights.claim: At each transition between monetary systems a toll is paid, and Hong Kong, gold vaults and stablecoins are the three locks where value comes to a halt - so the owners of those chokepoints capture the economics of fragmentation.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Points to a concrete basket for the fragmentation trade: Hong Kong assets, physical gold and the stablecoin/vaulting infrastructure.
insights.quote: At each transition from one system to another, a toll is paid: Hong Kong, gold vaults, and stablecoins are the locks where value comes to a halt.
insights.locator: At each transition from one system to another

insights.claim: There is no longer any single currency fulfilling all three monetary functions globally, and there likely will not be one for a very long time - instead there are three currencies (the US dollar, the renminbi and gold) linked by sluices.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The base case is a tri-polar monetary system, so allocate across all three legs rather than betting on a single dollar-successor.
insights.quote: There is no longer, at the global level, a currency that fulfills all three functions, and there will likely not be one for a very long time.

themes.theme: Trade implications: structural steepener, gold, Hong Kong

insights.claim: The US yield curve must steepen structurally because the two ends now have divorced customer bases: the front end has a price-insensitive buyer as each stablecoin issued automatically buys a Treasury bond, while the long end has only natural sellers as central banks rotate to gold and GCC savings rotate to equity.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A direct, mechanical steepener thesis independent of the inflation outlook - the cleanest expression is 2s10s or 5s30s steepeners.
insights.quote: The curve must therefore steepen structurally, not in anticipation of inflation but through a divorce between two customer groups
insights.locator: First, on the American curve

insights.claim: If US authorities eventually cap long yields through curve control or regulatory constraint, that will be an admission that financial repression has begun and the signal for the final migration of savings into gold, or possibly the renminbi.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Gives a specific, observable trigger for the terminal gold trade: any move toward yield-curve control or forced domestic bank buying of Treasuries.
insights.quote: the day when we reach a ceiling along the way, through curve control or regulatory constraint, it will be an admission that financial repression has begun, and the signal of the final migration towards gold
insights.locator: and the day when we reach a ceiling along the way

insights.claim: The overall configuration is bearish long-dated bonds and bearish the US dollar, bullish gold, and above all bullish Hong Kong assets.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The explicit portfolio conclusion: underweight duration and USD, overweight gold, with Hong Kong assets as the highest-conviction expression.
insights.quote: None of this is bullish for long-dated bonds, or for the US dollar. This new set-up is bullish for gold. But most of all, it might be very bullish Hong Kong assets.
insights.locator: None of this is bullish for long-dated bonds

insights.claim: The unit-of-account function remains American and is the last bastion of dollar hegemony, which is why the battle over AI billing could prove decisive for the currency order.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Watch the currency of AI service invoicing as the single most informative indicator for the dollar's remaining structural franchise.
insights.quote: The unit of account, the stickiest, remains American; it is the last bastion. Which is why the battle over AI billing could prove very important.
insights.locator: 5) Conclusion
